messages:
maya: Heads-up: small but visible hedging bump (~1.6%) after the latest policy push. Traces show routing decisions diverging between replicas during snapshot handoff.
leo: saw it in staging too. Pattern: some routers pick new-epoch low-cost variants while others stick to old-epoch latency-optimized variants -> request fans out.
frank: quick brainstorming: we already have epoch headers, fingerprints, token-buckets, compatibility blooms in various RFCs. Can we synthesize a coordinated approach that avoids layering complexity?
anya: yes. proposal: three coordinated runtime primitives:
1) canonical snapshot fingerprint (server-side HMAC over canonical proto) -> published with snapshot metadata
2) lightweight bloom compatibility published alongside fingerprint for fast accept/reject
3) soft admission token-buckets per-region-per-epoch to smooth capacity handoff
Combined with a per-tenant knob: routing.epoch_mode = ["allow","prefer","strict"].
leo: runtime sketch: on publish -> policy-service emits {snapshot_id, fingerprint, compact_bloom, capability_bits, seed_admission_tokens_by_region}. Routers fast-path: if candidate.fingerprint in bloom && capability_bits match tenant -> accept; else fallback. Admission: routers seed local token-bucket for new epoch using seed_admission_tokens_by_region and only consume small fraction for early traffic.
maya: probes: suppress probe-triggered hedges during rollouts by tagging probes with origin_fingerprint & origin_epoch. If probe.origin_fingerprint < local_fingerprint - 1 or origin_epoch < local_epoch - 1 then ignore probe as a hedge trigger.
frank: semantics: if bloom says 'possible match' we route and asynchronously run a deep-compat check. If deep-check later rejects, we emit corrective_decision for future requests but don't retroactively change the current response. No silent retries for now.
leo: bounded waits: prefer mode will wait up to 8ms for same-fingerprint candidate, strict up to 25ms + optional quorum requirement. If no match within bound, fall back according to tenant setting. Keep waits observable via metrics.
anya: metrics to add: routing.fingerprint_mismatch_count, routing.bloom_fast_accept_rate, routing.deepcheck_reject_rate, epoch.admission.tokens_consumed, routing.hedge_rate_by_epoch_and_region, routing.epoch_wait_ms.p95. Console dashboards + alerts if hedges > baseline +1.0%.
maya: rollout plan: 1) enable canonical fingerprint + bloom publish in staging (non-breaking), 2) update router fast-path to honor bloom + probe suppression behind flag, 3) run mixed-epoch+fingerprint sim for 24h, 4) canary 1% tenants with prefer mode, 5) if stable, enable token-bucket admission globally and ramp strict canary.
frank: safety: keep a global auto-fallback timeout for the quorum handshake. If quorum not achieved in T_quorum (default 10s) auto-activate in prefer mode and page if impact_estimate > threshold. Also GC bloom state after TTL to avoid memory bloat.
leo: tests: unit canonicalizer parity across langs, sim with recent traffic, critical-prompt eval for incompatible snapshots (fail publish if regression). Add e2e canary dashboard.
anya: action items:
- policy-service: implement canonicalizer + publish fingerprint+bloom+seeded_admission (leo)
- router runtime: bloom fast-path + probe suppression + admission token-bucket + bounded prefer/strict waits (maya)
- telemetry: add metrics and Console panels + hedges alert (frank)
I'll draft an RFC addendum with sequence diagrams and sim config by EOD.
ops-bot: "policy-compiler: fingerprint+bloom feature flag enabled in staging at 2026-06-30T14:02:00Z"
maya: thanks. ping to pair on the router changes. :thumbsup:
